title: Inter-Inter-Mezzo
program_note:
Intermezzi in the 19th century were short character pieces, originally intended to go between other (usually larger) pieces.   Inter-Inter-Mezzo, for solo piano, is two such pieces in one.  The first — shorter — piece may be thought of as the “outer” personality, or the outer character.  The second — longer — piece also presents the outer character, but includes a glimpse of the “inner” character within it, as a piece-within-a-piece.  The outer piece is characterized by mostly-constant downward gestures, cycling through a large six-and-one-half octave mode, and by a compression of those gestures toward an urgent close.  The inner piece is characterized by a mix of gentle upward gestures, encompassing a simpler (six-note) mode, and precipitous upward and downward runs, encompassing an eight-note mode.

Inter-Inter-Mezzo was originally a solo piano work, composed for and commissioned by Suzana Bartal, and completed in 2015.  It was premiered by Suzana Bartal in Paris in November, 2015.

David S. Lefkowitz

7 January, 2017

Los Angeles, California
